reason: The only priest explicitly mentioned in this text fragment is Jethro (יִתְרוֹ), identified as a 'priest of Midian' (כֹהֵן מִדְיָן). He is consistently depicted favorably: Moses goes out to meet him with respect, they embrace and kiss, they share a meal together, Jethro offers wise counsel that Moses accepts and implements, and he makes burnt offerings and sacrifices to God. The text treats him with honor and his advice improves Israel's governance structure. This positive portrayal indicates favorable depiction of the priest mentioned.
